A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FlexCAD work and contain readable main text, tables, figures, and appendices. The additional page in v2 results from reference reflow; the scientific content can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original CAD-generation experiments, human evaluations, and ablations in Section 4 and the appendices, including results for FlexCAD in Tables 1–7.

after.justification: v2 retains the original CAD-generation experiments, human evaluations, ablations, and appendix results reported in v1.

M1.justification: The structured CAD representation, hierarchy-aware masking, LoRA fine-tuning, unified training, and inference procedure remain unchanged. Grammar corrections in illustrated prompts do not change the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use DeepCAD and retain the same hierarchy-specific generation tasks, iterative editing demonstrations, and unconditional generation task. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains GPT-4o, SkexGen, and Hnc-cad as comparators; Table 7 retains SkexGen and Hnc-cad. The comparison methods and ablation configurations are unchanged.

E3.justification: The data split, preprocessing, training settings, metrics, and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Both retain the 1,000-input comparison with ten predictions per input and the human evaluation using seven raters and 950 image pairs per method.

E4.justification: Both retain the same model and masking ablations, circle-representation comparison, sampling sensitivity analysis, human-rating distributions, iterative editing examples, and failure analysis. No supplementary analysis is added or revised.

E5.justification: Both report three-run averages for Table 1 and inference-time averages over 1,000 runs in Appendix A.6. There are no changes to seed information, uncertainty reporting, or statistical testing.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain the same numerical entries, and the qualitative outputs and findings are unchanged. For example, FlexCAD's Table 1 prediction validity remains 93.4% for sketch-level generation and 93.3% for extrusion-level generation.

T1.justification: The CAD hierarchy definitions in Section 3.1 and parameter definitions in Appendix A.1 are unchanged. Neither version introduces additional theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims of unified controllable CAD generation across hierarchies, novelty in using LLMs for this purpose, and improved generation quality and controllability.

C2.justification: The explanations of pretraining and unified-training benefits, sampling tradeoffs, inference costs, and failures potentially caused by data imbalance are retained. Appendix A.6 preserves the same limitations and future directions.

D1.justification: The abstract changes the promised code location from microsoft/CADGeneration/FlexCAD to microsoft/FlexCAD. Both still state that code will be available, so the PDFs do not establish a release. Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, and timing information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and bibliography are unchanged, as is the positioning relative to earlier CAD-generation methods and LLM research. The added funding acknowledgement does not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 updates the publication header to ICLR 2025, changes the Microsoft affiliation to Microsoft Research, adds a funding acknowledgement, and corrects 'Generate an string' in illustrated prompts. The scientific prose and narrative structure otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Illustrated prompts in Figure 4 and Figures 10–16 receive small text and typesetting edits. The abstract and references reflow around the revised link and added acknowledgement; the figures and tables retain their substantive content and organization.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the same scientific account, experimental evidence, and limitations, including all appendix results. The grammar fixes, publication and funding metadata, and revised promised code location are small updates; they do not establish a meaningful overall quality gain or loss.
